headline: Federal Aviation Administration Resolves Nationwide Flight Grounding
seoTitle: US Flights Resume After Nationwide Grounding
metaDescription: US aviation authorities have lifted a nationwide ground stop following a major communication failure that disrupted travel for 1.5 million passengers.
aiSummaryBullets: A widespread communication failure at the Federal Aviation Administration led to a national ground stop for all departing US flights.
The disruption resulted in the cancellation of approximately 8,000 flights and affected roughly 1.5 million travelers across the country.
Operations have gradually resumed, though airlines continue to manage a backlog of cancellations and residual travel delays.
aiContextParagraph: On November 13, 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an unprecedented nationwide ground stop for all departing US flights due to a significant communication failure within its air traffic control systems. This event marks the second time such a comprehensive grounding has been ordered in US airspace since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The incident caused widespread chaos, leading to nearly 6,000 flight cancellations on Friday and an additional 2,000 following the initial stoppage. Approximately 1.5 million passengers were impacted by the event, which authorities have attributed to outdated infrastructure. While flight operations have since begun to resume, airlines are still working to normalize schedules after the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. Transportation officials are currently reviewing the incident to address the underlying technological vulnerabilities revealed by the sudden network crisis.
whyItIsViral: The event generated significant interest due to its scale, marking the longest nationwide US flight grounding in 25 years and affecting 1.5 million passengers.
